title: The monsoon wait
hook: four months of rain stop the story: chaturmas, when Vishnu is said to rest
carry: chaturmas: waiting is a sacred season
tomorrow: the rains end. does Sugriva keep his promise?

segments.voice: Yesterday: Sugriva, the arrow from behind the trees, and Vali's case, heard out loud. Dharma is subtle.

Everything is finally ready. It's been a week of running: a faked cry in the forest, a line in the dust, a beggar at the door, a flying chariot, an old bird who fell, Rama broken, Shabari's berries, two monkey brothers and one arrow. Now Rama has an army, and there's a new king on the throne of Kishkindha. Sugriva has promised to search the whole world for Sita. Go, go, go. And then it starts to rain. Not a shower. The monsoon. The whole story has to sit down and wait four months.
screen: `A WEEK OF RUNNING.` → `AN ARMY, FINALLY.` → `THEN IT RAINS.`

segments.voice: The rains close the roads. Paths turn to mud, rivers flood, armies stay home. Sugriva tells Rama they'll start the search when the rains end, so Rama and Lakshmana wait in a cave on a mountainside, watching the storm. And here Valmiki does something remarkable. In the middle of an adventure story, he stops and writes page after page about rain. Dark clouds lowering over the hills. Peacocks dancing. Rivers running brown and fast. Frogs waking. And it's all seen through the eyes of a miserable man: every beautiful thing reminds Rama of Sita. Lakshmana, again, is the steady one. This is the season for waiting, he tells his brother, in effect. When it turns, we move. Hindus still keep this season. They call it chaturmas, the four months, and it has a story of its own. It begins on an Ekadashi, an eleventh day of the moon, when Vishnu is said to lie down to sleep on the great serpent, and it ends on another Ekadashi, months later, when he wakes. Rama is honored as Vishnu's avatar, so in the sacred calendar, the God who came as Rama rests through the rains too. Holy wanderers stay in one place. Many people take a small vow or a simpler diet, and many families wait until Vishnu wakes to hold weddings. The waiting isn't wasted; it's part of the sacred year. When life gives you a season you can't hurry, a result, a recovery, a reply, the tradition doesn't call it lost time. It gives the wait a name, and something to keep while you're in it.
screen: `THE RAINS CLOSE THE ROADS.` · `VALMIKI STOPS TO PAINT THE STORM.` · `CHATURMAS: FOUR SACRED MONTHS.` · `VISHNU RESTS. THE WORLD WAITS.` · then, large: `WAITING IS A SACRED SEASON.`

segments.voice: Many Hindus begin chaturmas with a small vow: giving up one food, adding one prayer, one kindness a day. Think of something you're waiting for, and notice how the waiting sits in your body. Then choose one small thing to keep while you wait, a prayer or a daily kindness, and let the wait be a season, not a prison.
Chaturmas, the four months of the monsoon. The hero can't move, and Valmiki's long poem of the storm.
Your line: chaturmas. Waiting is a sacred season. That's the whole week, and the long wait. Tomorrow the rain stops.

howItsDone: Many Hindus observe chaturmas, the four months from Devshayani Ekadashi, when Vishnu is said to go to sleep, to Prabodhini (Dev Uthani) Ekadashi, when he wakes, as a slower, more devotional season: renunciates stay in one place, many take small vows or simplify their food, and weddings are often held after it.

chaturmas.meaning: the four months of the monsoon, a season to slow down

Valmiki.meaning: the poet traditionally credited with the first Ramayana

Kishkindha.meaning: the monkey kingdom where Sugriva now rules

Sugriva.meaning: the new monkey king, who promised to search for Sita

Ekadashi.meaning: the eleventh day of the moon's waxing or waning, kept for Vishnu

Vishnu.meaning: the preserver; Rama is honored as his avatar

Dev Uthani Ekadashi.meaning: the Ekadashi when Vishnu is said to wake, ending chaturmas

Bal Vihar.meaning: a Hindu Sunday school for children, often at the mandir
